hints.title: Reverse Thinking
hints.text: Instead of starting from an array of 1s and building target, work backwards from target to all 1s.

hints.title: Largest Element Must Be Reduced
hints.text: The largest number in target was formed by summing the rest of the array. Let rest = total_sum - max_val.

hints.title: Modulo Speedup
hints.text: When max_val is much larger than rest, use modulo: prev = max_val % rest. If rest == 1, it always succeeds.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def isPossible(self, target: list[int]) -> bool:
        total = sum(target)
        max_heap = [-x for x in target]
        heapq.heapify(max_heap)
        while True:
            largest = -heapq.heappop(max_heap)
            rest = total - largest
            if largest == 1 or rest == 1:
                return True
            if rest == 0 or largest <= rest or largest % rest == 0:
                return False
            prev = largest % rest
            total = rest + prev
            heapq.heappush(max_heap, -prev)
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Subtracting rest repeatedly one by one causes time limit exceeded when target has large values like 10^9.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Using Euclidean modulo reduction speeds up consecutive subtractions to logarithmic steps.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate applies reverse simulation with modulo Euclidean division.
complexity.notes: Edge case rest == 1 guarantees success because (largest % 1) reduces to 1 in one multi-step subtraction.
